nodes.description: Confirmed or suspected autism spectrum disorder in about six in ten individuals.

evidence.reference_title: De novo and inherited variants in ZNF292 underlie a neurodevelopmental disorder with features of autism spectrum disorder.
evidence.snippet: A confirmed or suspected diagnosis of ASD was present in 17/27 (62%) individuals and of ADHD in 9/27 (33%) (Table 1, Figure S5).

nodes.description: ZNF292 binds the promoters of neuronal and synaptic genes. With reduced ZNF292, its direct targets controlling neuronal differentiation and synapse formation are upregulated in progenitors, while targets promoting interneuron maturation, including other neurodevelopmental disorder genes, are downregulated in interneurons.

evidence.reference_title: De novo and inherited variants in ZNF292 underlie a neurodevelopmental disorder with features of autism spectrum disorder.
evidence.snippet: ZNF292 encodes a highly conserved zinc finger protein that acts as a transcription factor and is highly expressed in the developing human brain supporting its critical role in neurodevelopment.

evidence.reference_title: Requirements for the neurodevelopmental disorder-associated gene ZNF292 in human cortical interneuron development and function.
evidence.snippet: In progenitors, genome-wide occupancy and transcriptomic analyses identify direct target genes controlling neuronal differentiation and synapse formation that are upregulated upon ZNF292 deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Requirements for the neurodevelopmental disorder-associated gene ZNF292 in human cortical interneuron development and function.
evidence.snippet: By contrast, deficiency in interneurons compromises ZNF292 genome-wide association with and causes downregulation of direct target genes promoting interneuron maturation and function, including other NDD genes.

nodes.description: ZNF292-deficient cortical interneurons stay immature, express interneuron markers less often, produce smaller sodium and potassium currents, respond more strongly to GABA and show signs of hyperactivity. The authors suggest that some of these defects may contribute to the human disorder; the link to patient phenotypes has not been tested.

evidence.reference_title: Requirements for the neurodevelopmental disorder-associated gene ZNF292 in human cortical interneuron development and function.
evidence.snippet: ZNF292-deficient interneurons also exhibit altered channel activities, elevated GABA responsiveness, and hallmarks of neuronal hyperactivity.

evidence.reference_title: Requirements for the neurodevelopmental disorder-associated gene ZNF292 in human cortical interneuron development and function.
evidence.snippet: Together, the results of this work define neurodevelopmental requirements for ZNF292, some of which may contribute to pathogenic ZNF292 mutation-related NDDs.

nodes.description: Present in nearly all individuals; in the defining cohort it was mild in 11 of 27, moderate in 6 and severe in 3.

evidence.reference_title: De novo and inherited variants in ZNF292 underlie a neurodevelopmental disorder with features of autism spectrum disorder.
evidence.snippet: Of the individuals with ID, delays were mild in 11/27 (40%), moderate in 6/27 (22%) and severe in 3/27 (11%).

evidence.reference_title: De Novo ZNF292 Variants Cause Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Short Stature: A Clinical Case Series of Eight Individuals.
evidence.snippet: All individuals exhibited global developmental delay, intellectual disability, and short stature.

nodes.description: ZNF292-deficient cortical interneuron progenitors exit the cell cycle and differentiate early, upregulating neuronal and synaptic genes ahead of time.

evidence.reference_title: Requirements for the neurodevelopmental disorder-associated gene ZNF292 in human cortical interneuron development and function.
evidence.snippet: ZNF292-deficient progenitors undergo precocious differentiation but subsequently exhibit compromised interneuron maturation and function.

evidence.reference_title: De novo and inherited variants in ZNF292 underlie a neurodevelopmental disorder with features of autism spectrum disorder.
evidence.snippet: We identified 23 de novo predicted loss of function (pLoF) variants (pLoFs; nonsense, frameshift, or splice) in 27 families and one transmitted (i.e., inherited from an affected mother) pLoF in one family (18–003) for a total of 24 putatively pathogenic variants in ZNF292 (Table S1, Figure 1) in 28 families.

evidence.reference_title: De Novo ZNF292 Variants Cause Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Short Stature: A Clinical Case Series of Eight Individuals.
evidence.snippet: Seven de novo variants in ZNF292 were identified, including two nonsense and five frameshift variants

nodes.description: Disease variants are nonsense, frameshift or splice variants, mostly in exon 8, which encodes the large DNA-binding domain. Because exon 8 is the last exon, most of these variants are predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay. The authors of the defining cohort left open whether the disease arises from haploinsufficiency or from a truncated protein with gain-of-function or dominant-negative activity.

evidence.reference_title: De novo and inherited variants in ZNF292 underlie a neurodevelopmental disorder with features of autism spectrum disorder.
evidence.snippet: Most variants (22/24) are located in exon 8, the last and largest exon of ZNF292, which encodes a large DNA binding domain of the protein (Figure 1).

evidence.reference_title: De novo and inherited variants in ZNF292 underlie a neurodevelopmental disorder with features of autism spectrum disorder.
evidence.snippet: The two most likely possibilities by which pLoF might underlie disease are escape from nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), leading to expression of a truncated protein that has either a gain of function or dominant negative effect, or simple haploinsufficiency.

evidence.reference_title: De Novo ZNF292 Variants Cause Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Short Stature: A Clinical Case Series of Eight Individuals.
evidence.snippet: As a sequence-specific DNA-binding protein, ZNF292 recognizes and binds to the promoters of neuronal and synaptic genes, thereby directly regulating the expression of multiple neurodevelopmental disorder risk genes

nodes.description: H9 human embryonic stem cells carrying CRISPR interference constructs that lower ZNF292 to roughly heterozygous levels, differentiated into cortical interneuron progenitors and neurons.
